newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on pre-election cash demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on pre-election cash demand.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 70 basis points at 21.20 percent early Tuesday, even though the peso was firmer as the approach of midterm elections boosted demand for liquidity, dealers said.
"An opposition victory has already been discounted to an extent, but there are some who prefer to go liquid," a dealer said.
Mexican elections will be held on July 6 to renew the entire lower house of Congress, one-quarter of the Senate, several state governors and the first poll for Mexico City mayor in modern times.
Fixed-income analysts said they expected pressures to continue on overnight rates, but did not foresee them reaching as high as Monday's peak of 22.70 percent.

"Paper was in demand towards the close yesterday after rates had shot up. We should see a calmer market today, but the run up to elections could spur jitters and volatility in the coming days," one analyst said.
Dealers said inflation data for the first half of June expected from the Banco de Mexico would likely come too late to have much impact on the market.
"Inflation data will come out very later, and I don't feel they will have much effect on the market today, although they could calm it down a little tomorrow," a dealer said.
A Reuters survey MEX22 of 13 financial houses forecast on average an increase of 0.47 percent in the Consumer Price Index for June 1-15.
Overnight rates on bank paper had meanwhile risen 40 basis points to 22.40 percent.
Liquidity of 59 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
